description: Few-shot SQL examples for improved generation accuracy

examples.question: What are the top 10 selling products?
examples.sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(s.total_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN sales s ON p.product_id = s.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 10

examples.question: Show monthly revenue for the last year
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', s.sale_date) AS month, SUM(s.total_price) AS monthly_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id) AS total_orders FROM sales s WHERE s.sale_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s.sale_date) ORDER BY month ASC

examples.question: Which city generated the highest sales?
examples.sql: SELECT r.city, SUM(s.total_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(s.sale_id) AS transaction_count FROM sales s JOIN regions r ON s.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY r.city ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1

examples.question: What is the average order value by customer segment?
examples.sql: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC

examples.question: Show the distribution of customers by age group
examples.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN age BETWEEN 18 AND 25 THEN '18-25' WHEN age BETWEEN 26 AND 35 THEN '26-35' WHEN age BETWEEN 36 AND 45 THEN '36-45' WHEN age BETWEEN 46 AND 55 THEN '46-55' WHEN age BETWEEN 56 AND 65 THEN '56-65' ELSE '65+' END AS age_group, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY age_group ORDER BY age_group

examples.question: What is the order cancellation rate by month?
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders, ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled' THEN 1 END)::DECIMAL / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS cancellation_rate FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month

examples.question: Which employees have the most sales?
examples.sql: SELECT e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee_name, e.department, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_handled, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.department ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10

examples.question: Compare sales performance across regions
examples.sql: SELECT r.region_name, r.state, SUM(s.total_price) AS total_sales, AVG(s.total_price) AS avg_sale_value, COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id) AS unique_orders FROM regions r JOIN sales s ON r.region_id = s.region_id GROUP BY r.region_name, r.state ORDER BY total_sales DESC

examples.question: What are the most popular product categories?
examples.sql: SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(s.sale_id) AS total_sales, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_units_sold, SUM(s.total_price) AS total_revenue FROM categories c JOIN products p ON c.category_id = p.category_id JOIN sales s ON p.product_id = s.product_id GROUP BY c.category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

examples.question: Show customer acquisition trend over time
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS new_customers, SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (ORDER BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)) AS cumulative_customers FROM customers GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) ORDER BY month
